verdict.headline: Long-term bond yields hold just below their 2002 high as the September jobs report nears
verdict.label: Pre-market: S&P 500 futures +0.4%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.6%; 30Y ~5.618% (+1 bp, 2002 high 5.644%), 10Y ~5.243%, 2Y ~4.79% (-9 bp Thursday); Oct hike odds ~35%; Brent ~$102; DXY ~101.9; gold ~$4,179; BTC ~$86,460; Hang Seng -2.6%.
verdict.rationale_short: The thirty-year Treasury yield is at about 5.618%, 2.6 basis points under its 2002 high, with the September jobs report due at 8:30 a.m. Thursday's pullback did not carry overnight. The short end did the moving: the two-year fell 9 basis points on Thursday to about 4.79% as October hike odds fell to about 35%, widening the gap to the thirty-year to roughly 83 basis points. Short yields falling with the Fed path while long yields hold near 24-year highs says the pressure on long bonds is not mainly about the Fed; oil near $102 and government-bond selling abroad are still in place. Economists expect about 90,000 jobs. A thirty-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say it is fading.
verdict.lede_short: The 30-year Treasury yield sits about 5.62% this morning, just under its 2002 high, as the September jobs report arrives. Two-year yields fell on Thursday with October hike odds while long yields barely moved, which says the long-end pressure is not mainly about the Fed. A 30-year close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say it is fading.

supporting_data.label: The thirty-year rose about 1 basis point to 5.618% and the ten-year held near 5.243% before payrolls — long yields are holding Thursday's levels rather than extending the pullback.

The two-year fell 9 basis points on Thursday to just under 4.80% while the ten-year closed about 4 basis points lower — the curve steepened, so falling hike odds are reaching short yields but not long ones.
Economists expect about 90,000 September jobs, unemployment at 4.1% and hourly earnings up 0.3%, after August's 162,000 — a print near consensus would be a slowdown, not a contraction.
October hike odds stood near 35% on CME FedWatch at Thursday's close, from about 71% a week earlier — the jobs report decides whether that decline continues or reverses.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 2.6% to 23,972.29, its lowest since July, on its first session back from holiday — it priced a week of higher global yields in one day while US futures rose.
Nike fell 9.6% pre-market to about $31.79 after guiding fiscal 2027 revenue down by a high single-digit percentage — the clearest sign yet this week that demand outside AI is weakening.

watchlist_mentions.note: Third-quarter deliveries due today against a company-compiled consensus of 461,974, down 7.1% from a year earlier; estimates range from about 422,000 to 482,000.
Up about 3% over 24 hours to about $86,460 ahead of payrolls, rising with stock futures while the dollar sits near its 2026 high.

trade_setups.thesis: The thirty-year sits 2.6 basis points under its 2002 high while two-year yields fall with hike odds; payrolls test whether the long end responds to the Fed path at all.
trade_setups.entry: Thirty-year ~5.618% between the 2002 high of 5.644% above and 5.44% below.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above 5.644% would resume the rise; a close under 5.44% would say it is fading. A soft print with the thirty-year still above 5.6% would say the pressure is not about the Fed.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's payrolls through next Wednesday's Fed minutes

trade_setups.thesis: Nike's guide and General Mills at a 52-week low point to weaker spending outside AI; Tesla deliveries are today's next read.
trade_setups.entry: Tesla consensus 461,974 deliveries, range about 422,000 to 482,000; Nike ~$31.79 pre-market.
trade_setups.invalidation: Deliveries above consensus alongside firm payrolls would weaken the read.

trade_setups.thesis: Hong Kong fell 2.6% to a July low as US futures rose; the US market has stood apart from the global response to higher yields.
trade_setups.invalidation: An S&P 500 close under 7,600 with the thirty-year above 5.644% would mean US stocks are following the rest of the world; a close above 7,666.45 with yields under the line would keep the gap open.
